newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Balts, Poland, Ukraine concerned about Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Balts, Poland, Ukraine concerned about Belarus.

text.p: Poland, Ukraine and three former Soviet Baltic states expressed concern on Tuesday at the situation in Belarus where President Aleksander Lukashenko has been blasted by international watchdogs for human-rights abuses.
"Today we discussed very intensively the situation in Belarus -- the democratic or non-democratic processes there," Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis told a joint news conference in Tallinn.
"We agreed that we must talk with Belarus and we must express our concern about the situation there," Ulmanis added.

He had just taken part in a special regional summit with presidents Aleksander Kwasniewski of Poland, Leonid Kuchma of Ukraine, Lennart Meri of Estonia and Algirdas Brazauskas of Lithuania. All the countries except Estonia border on Belarus.
Lukashenko has come under constant criticism from the United States, European institutions and human-rights groups over his authoritarian rule in the ex-Soviet republic of 10 million people.
Lukashenko, who last November won sweeping powers in a controversial constitutional referendum, has been keeping pressure on political opposition, independent trade unions and the media.
Several opposition newspapers were forced to move to move to Lithuania to be printed.
A spokesman for Kuchma said the five leaders discussed the possibility of a joint meeting with Lukashenko.
"The presidents favoured the idea of not isolating Belarus. An absence of dialogue is much worse than dialogue itself," spokesman Dmytro Markov told reporters.

"There can be no isolationist approach towards Belarus but at the same time no one can calmly watch cases of the violation of human rights...The presidents backed the democratic development of Belarus," he added.

Lukashenko signed a union charter with Russian President Boris Yeltsin last week in Moscow but has retreated from the idea of creating a single state with its huge neighbour to the east, an idea that Moscow strongly backs.
